claims.statement: TalonHost is a long-running host for a single assistant that owns and jointly starts/stops the agent runtime, channel adapters, and an optional cron scheduler in one asyncio event loop.

Talon is an experimental, alpha-status runtime that ships no production security controls (no complete HITL policy, channel admin gates, sandbox isolation, or multi-tenant boundaries), and channel access must be treated as direct access to the operator's agent, credentials, MCP tools, and local host.

The host stops its background loop and cancels all in-flight agent work and pending approval/authorization futures before stopping channels in reverse order, then scheduler and runtime; its stop event is set by request_shutdown or installed signals.

A new inbound message replaces an active turn in the same conversation: Talon cancels it, recovers the latest checkpoint where possible, and uses generations to prevent the cancelled turn from delivering stale output; separate conversations can run concurrently.
The /new command starts a fresh conversation thread by cancelling the current run and incrementing a persisted per-conversation reset counter that is appended to the agent thread id.

The AgentRuntime protocol (start/stop/invoke/recover_interrupted) decouples the host from the agent implementation, and Talon provides EchoAgentRuntime (returns request text) and DeepAgentRuntime (a real Deep Agents graph).

DeepAgentRuntime.start builds the Deep Agents graph via create_deep_agent, and invoke uses a thread_id equal to the conversation id with a per-invocation recursion limit; it defaults to in-memory checkpoints while standard model-backed CLI boot supplies persistent SQLite ConversationSaver.

DeepAgentRuntime retries transient provider, parse, context-limit, and transport errors with exponential backoff, and sends continuation nudges then a force-summary prompt when the graph returns empty text.

DeepAgentRuntime executes shell/filesystem work through a non-virtual LocalShellBackend rooted at DEEPAGENTS_TALON_WORKSPACE (or the current directory) with a scrubbed child environment that drops secrets and env-hijack keys and replaces PATH with a fixed safe path.
Channel adapters implement the ChannelAdapter protocol; the host registers message and supported reaction callbacks so inbound events flow into receive_message and receive_reaction.
PersistentCronScheduler is a minute-granularity ticker that scans immediately, wakes on its tick interval or stop signal, runs due jobs, and logs a failed scan before retrying on the normal interval.

Before running a due cron job the scheduler claims the next interval via advance_next_run, records the outcome with mark_job_run, and suppresses delivery when output begins or ends with the [SILENT] sentinel.
CronJobStore persists assistant-scoped jobs to cron/jobs.json, including origin and outcome state, through atomic fsynced temporary-file replacement with 0600 permissions.
Agent-facing cron tools are exposed only when a cron store is supplied and are scoped to the current conversation origin through a context variable.
Because scheduled runs cannot surface interactive approval, a gated tool call under a cron trigger is auto-denied with an explanatory message rather than blocking the run.
On a channel-triggered tool-approval interrupt the host records a pending approval keyed by conversation and accepts a text or matching emoji decision only from the sender who started the run.

TalonConfig.from_env selects the assistant namespace from DEEPAGENTS_TALON_ASSISTANT_ID (or AGENT_ASSISTANT_ID), validates it as a safe path segment defaulting to 'default', and reads the model from DEEPAGENTS_TALON_MODEL/AGENT_MODEL.

The standard model-backed CLI persists conversation checkpoints and a channel/chat-scoped archive in checkpoints.sqlite through ConversationSaver, whereas DeepAgentRuntime used directly defaults to in-memory checkpoints.
A cancellation that does not finish within 30 seconds blocks that conversation until Talon restarts; a checkpoint-recovery failure instead permits a replacement turn with failure metadata.
Talon converts result Markdown media references to outbound channel attachments only when they resolve inside the configured outbound media root, and reports failed attachments in fallback text.

For channel-based MCP OAuth, Talon sends authorization URLs directly to the origin chat and accepts a callback only from the same sender, provider, and conversation; authorization values bypass model context and tracing.
The CLI attaches PersistentCronScheduler only when channels are configured, wiring scheduled invocation to TalonHost.run_scheduled_job and delivery to the originating channel.
TalonConfig ensures a namespaced per-assistant home and creates manifest, agent, cron, channel, and inbound-media directories with restrictive 0700 permissions.
The runtime stores channel history scope and cron origin in context variables around each invocation, allowing archive and cron tools to be request-scoped rather than global.
A delivery failure overwrites an otherwise successful cron generation outcome with an error in the persistent job record.

Talon's URI-selected history archive is namespaced by assistant ID, supports built-in SQLite, MongoDB, and PostgreSQL stores plus a trusted installed entry-point backend, while persistent checkpoints remain local.

Talon emits redacted structured talon_event logs and optionally emits local bounded agent activity logs; LangSmith tracing requires both LANGSMITH_TRACING and LANGSMITH_API_KEY and attaches assistant, conversation, and request metadata.

MCP tool refresh and explicit reload construct a replacement graph before replacing the active graph, so a failed tool reload leaves the prior graph usable; subagent reloads apply to later turns while active turns retain their captured graph.
The CLI configures channel logger verbosity from DEEPAGENTS_CODE_DEBUG or DEEPAGENTS_CODE_LOG_LEVEL, accepting DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, and CRITICAL values for the latter.
Talon startup binds callbacks before starting each channel and unwinds a partial startup by stopping the scheduler, started channels in reverse order, and runtime before reraising the error.
DeepAgentRuntime refuses to tear down graph/checkpointer resources if background workers outlive cancellation, while TalonHost logs the component stop failure and continues shutdown.
Every channel/chat conversation is keyed with its provider, becoming the lock key, LangGraph thread ID, and persisted reset-counter key; Talon deliberately does not migrate older bare keys.
A history reset persists a fresh reset counter before clearing the channel/chat archive, and rolls that counter back if clearing fails.

BackgroundSubagents are in-memory work owners with limits of 128 tasks, four active workers, and a one-hour task timeout; the host dispatches completed results through a follow-up turn and requeues them when a superseded reply was not delivered.
